generator.prompt: A Roman field barricade of sharpened stakes: five pairs of long double-pointed timber stakes, each pair crossed in an X and lashed at the middle with rope, threaded on one horizontal beam about two metres long, so that the points stand out on both sides like a cheval-de-frise, about one metre high. Weathered grey-brown wood with paler cut points and hemp rope. Single isolated static prop for a grounded painterly-realistic historical game set in the third century Roman world. Physically based aged materials, believable hand-made construction and strong readable silhouette, restrained surface detail, level base and complete geometry from every side. No environment, ground plane, decorative display plinth, modern materials, text, logos or people.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the battles in the desktop build at High, before and after
review.notes: Not the crossed pairs of stakes on one beam the prompt asked for, but a lattice of four sharpened horizontal beams on five sharpened uprights, braced and lashed with rope: a timber obstacle whose points face both ways, as the code-built barricade's stakes do. Kept: it reads as a field obstacle at once. A panel is 1.16 m long at 1.0 m high, so two stand side by side across the cell, east to west, spanning 2.3 m as the code-built barricade's 2 m do. Its thin stakes need their 2,939 triangles; the byte budget rose from 220,000 to 240,000 for them. In the game, in a crowded fight, its thin beams are harder to pick out than the code-built crossed stakes.
